data.cultural_impact: The name Mahidul conveys a strong connection to the Moon God, Maha (Great) Chandra, who holds significant representation in Hindu culture. Worship of the Moon God is prevalent throughout ancient texts - the Vedas and Upanishads, temple sites dedicated to him, lunar calendars, and even phases of the moon influencing rituals and ceremonies. In this name, Mahi adds the celestial significance while Dul is the revered deity, making it a name that resonates with the rich Hindu lunar lore.
data.spiritual_significance: Mahidul signifies reverence and devotion towards the Moon God, who symbolizes wisdom, imparting vast knowledge, and nourishment thanks to its role in the tides which bring fresh water to the earth. Producing light during the night, the Moon is also seen as a source of illumination, enlightening the darkest paths. With the name Mahidul, individuals express their inner yearning towards enlightenment and knowledge under the guidance of the Moon God.

historical_references.context: The name Mahidul is associated with the mythology of the god Shiva, where he is said to have taken the form of Mahidul to deceive the goddess Parvati.
